headline: Nothing to do today. Keep your SIPs running and leave your holdings alone.

reasons.title: Market mood
reasons.text: The Market Mood Index (Tickertape Market Mood Index) reads 59 of 100: greed. It was 19 a month ago and 76 a year ago. Investors often get most nervous near market lows and most confident near highs, so fear is usually the better time to invest and greed the time to be careful. That is a tendency, not a promise.

reasons.text: Its benchmark trades at a P/E of 31.4, against a typical 32.2 over the last ten years (a discount of 2%). Only 46% of the last ten years were cheaper, and 75% of the last five. Verdict: fair.

reasons.title: Trend
reasons.text: The Nifty (23,811) is 2.1% above its longer-term average (23,315) and 3.6% above its shorter-term one.

reasons.title: Your portfolio
reasons.text: Your mix is 6.8% below its most recent peak. That is an ordinary dip: this same mix has fallen as much as 35% before and recovered. Selling after a fall is how a temporary dip becomes a permanent loss.

reasons.title: Tomorrow
reasons.text: The short-term call for the next session is a coin-flip with a small tilt. It is useful context for a day trader and irrelevant for a long-term investor: don't buy or sell on it.

do_today: Keep your ₹1.10 lakh monthly SIP running. When prices are low it buys more units for the same money, which is exactly what a SIP is for.
If you have spare cash, there is no urgency; investing it gradually is fine.

Of the parts of the market your funds track, large + midcaps looks cheapest (cheap) and small caps the dearest (fair). If you add extra money, tilting it towards Mirae Asset Large & Midcap rather than Axis Small Cap follows that. Your regular SIPs can stay as they are.
Do not sell because of today's fall or tomorrow's red or green call.
if_you_sell: If you sold everything today you would pay about ₹2.37 lakh in tax, which is a strong reason not to sell on a market view.
Only sell money you will need within about three years; money for later goals is better left invested through the dip.

If you do need cash, sell from the older folio first (e.g. Axis Small Cap folio ): its gains are long-term, and the first ₹1.25 lakh of long-term gain each year is tax-free. The newer folios may still be short-term (taxed at 20%).
If you must raise a large sum, sell in two or three parts over a few weeks instead of in one go.
watch: If the Market Mood rises above 70 (extreme greed) and small caps are expensive against their own history, stop lump sums and think about booking some profit.
If it stays below 30, nothing changes: keep investing in stages. Recoveries from fear usually take months, not days.
If the Nifty closes back above its longer-term average (23,315) the trend has turned: invest any remaining instalments.
evidence: How much to trust this: on the Nifty 50 since 2012, months when it looked cheap against its own history were followed by a median 12.1% a year over three years, against 15.7% after dear months. So cheap or dear has told us little about average returns. It did tell us about the bad cases: the worst one-year result after cheap months was -8%, after dear months -26%. Treat the signals above as a reason for patience and for spreading out new money, not as a forecast.
disclaimer: Educational analysis of public market data, not personalised or SEBI-registered investment advice. It cannot know your goals, time horizon or income. Markets can stay cheap or expensive for long periods.
